methods.label: Express the sum using the roots
methods.explanation:
The condition that both roots exceed \(1\) suggests looking for factors of the form root minus \(1\). Let the roots be \(u\) and \(v\), so \(u>1\) and \(v>1\). Expanding the quadratic's factorization gives
\[
x^2+bx+c=(x-u)(x-v)
=x^2-(u+v)x+uv.
\]
Thus \(b=-(u+v)\) and \(c=uv\). Consequently,
\[
s=b+c+1=uv-u-v+1=(u-1)(v-1).
\]
Both factors are strictly positive, including when the roots are equal. Therefore \(s>0\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
